title: Researchers Build Entangled Bell Pair Spanning 100 Qubits With 59% Fidelity
key_facts: Researchers from IBM's Watson Research Center and the University of Wisconsin-Madison prepared an entangled Bell pair spanning 100 qubits on a superconducting processor
Fidelity 0.59 plus or minus 0.02, above the 0.5 threshold used to certify entanglement
Baseline dynamic-circuit method reached 0.39 plus or minus 0.01
Uses error detection and postselection, discarding runs that fail checks, to cut classical processing demands without extra qubits
Also prepared W states up to 20 qubits, with fidelity gains of about 0.2
Paper: Resilience Beyond the Light Cone: Error-Detected Primitives for Practical Dynamic Circuits (arXiv 2609.08925), by Smith, Pokharel, Maurya and Takita
Preprint; the article does not mention peer review
quote_evidence: Entanglement measures now reach a fidelity of 0.59 when creating a long-range Bell pair spanning 100 qubits; this exceeds the established entanglement certification threshold of 0.5.
Achieving substantial improvements relies heavily on postselection, discarding unsuccessful attempts.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows long-range entanglement on real hardware, with a cost: many runs are thrown away.
event_date: not stated (arXiv number suggests a September 2026 submission)
notes: Article names the affiliation as Watson Research Centre; read as IBM's Thomas J. Watson Research Center is not confirmed in text, so wording stays close to the article.
